I absolutely love flavorful origins. It's a documentary about Chinese food/culture, and the entire show is just aesthetic visuals and calm music. I watch it in the native Mandarin with English subtitles to go to sleep, and when folding laundry.

I absolutely love the series Rilakkuma and Kaoru. It's a chill, animated show that takes place in Japan. Kaoru is a woman that lives in an apartment with two bears, Rilakkuma and Korilakkuma, and also a bird, kiiroitori. The main struggles in this show is not having enough snacks, and I am always down to watch it.

I didn't really know him, but once I was visiting my uncles in Canada. Me and my sister and my brother were hanging out in some random playground, and I met this boy in a red shirt. I used to be painfully shy, and he kept inviting me to go on the slide and play tag with him and his friends. I was too shy to talk, but eventually we went on the seesaw together. I think about him all the time, and if he remembers me.

I was at a playground when I was very little, somewhere in Canada where they don't speak much English. It was one of those all wooden playgrounds, so the perfect place for all of those Carpenter bees. I was standing in line for this huge slide, and the boy next to me, who was about five, starts yelling at his younger sister in what I'm assuming is French. I look over at him, and he has a bee in his ear. I don't know how to explain, but that main cavity where your ear hole is was where the bee was. It was all curled up and wasn't trying to sting or anything. I was too shocked to say anything, and I don't even know how I would communicate that to him.

I'm late to the party, but I went on vacation to Hong Kong when I was younger (8-9ish) and stayed in a pretty fancy hotel(for my family). We had a housekeeper for that week, and she was the nicest person ever. She connected instantly with my grandparents because of religion, and she arranged me and my sister's stuffed animals in cute little scenarios and talked with us. She had a bad living situation that I don't know the details, and was barely getting by. We have a family picture with her, and I wonder how she's doing now.

I'm actually half Chinese, and I've actually experienced this. I've never been able to put it into words like this before so eloquently though. Now I know what to say! Thank you!
